summary: Reference article for building List COMP interfaces with Python callbacks, table/row/column/cell attributes, DAT or dictionary-backed content, and explicit state management for rollover, select, radio, focus, and edit behavior.

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Docked callback DAT that defines initialize and event functions for the List COMP

key_params.name: onInitTable
key_params.note: Initializes table-wide attributes such as text justification or borders

key_params.name: onInitCol
key_params.note: Initializes column attributes such as width and stretch behavior

key_params.name: onInitRow
key_params.note: Initializes row attributes such as background color

key_params.name: onInitCell
key_params.note: Initializes per-cell text and formatting from a DAT, dictionary, or other source

key_params.name: onRollover
key_params.note: Updates visual state while the cursor moves across cells

key_params.name: onSelect
key_params.note: Handles mouse down/up selection state and can run custom scripts

key_params.name: storage
key_params.note: Stores current list state, selected row, or dependent content dictionaries between callbacks

key_params.name: rows
key_params.note: Usually driven from the source table or content collection length

key_params.name: cols
key_params.note: Usually driven from source table width or header dictionary length

key_params.name: reset
key_params.note: Runs the initialize callbacks again after callback or data changes

key_concepts: Build a List COMP is the official callback-construction guide for List COMP interfaces rather than a separate creatable operator.
List initialization runs in table, column, row, then cell order through onInitTable, onInitCol, onInitRow, and onInitCell.
Event callbacks such as onRollover, onSelect, onRadio, onFocus, and onEdit drive interactive list behavior.
Rollover and select workflows must restore prior visual state, often by saving row state in Python storage.
Folder DATs, Python lists, dictionaries, and dependency storage can feed data-backed cell text and dimensions.
common_gotchas: Build a List COMP is a how-to article for List COMP, so promote it as callback knowledge rather than as a separate creatable operator when planning networks.
Initialize callbacks run on load or reset and must be kept deterministic because they rebuild table, row, column, and cell attributes.
Rollover and selection callbacks need to restore previous visual state; otherwise rows can stay highlighted after the cursor leaves.
When using dictionaries or Python lists as content, store them on the List COMP and provide safe fetch defaults for missing storage.
Cell, row, and column indices are zero-based; header-row logic needs explicit checks such as row == 0.
Large lists can become callback-heavy, so avoid doing expensive filesystem or network work directly in cell callbacks.
